clues: This chief town sits near the edge of its land, close to the next land over. Wide flat grass lands stretch far off to the north of town.
High hills to the south of town act like a wall and block the worst weather. In the cold months, thick fog can hang over the streets for days.
In 1825, a khan's men built a fort here to watch the trade roads. The fort let them hold the roads and claim tribute from the Kyrgyz tribes.
For much of the last age, this town bore the name of a Red war chief born here. In 1991 it took back a new form of its first name.
This city is the capital of Kyrgyzstan, in the heart of Asia. Grand halls of pale marble and broad tree lined roads fill its core.
